citation.authors: Miao Y, Xuerong T, Yiyue X
citation.title: A Study of Craniofacial Structure of normal occlusion in the South of China

secondHand.via: Moate & Darendeliler 2002, Tables I, III and IV

curation.notes: Compared 2026-10-08: norms:compare a vs b exit 1, 91 differences (logs/task9a2-compare-<id>.log). Every mean and SD of both extractors re-read from the page images (PDF pp. 2-6 = journal pp. 20-24), and the settled file checked by script against a third, independent reading of the pages (the table in sets.test.ts). Decisions: (0) Source text normalised to one pattern giving table, page, row and column with sex and age (a and b worded it differently; prose only). Adult rows: a gave [18, 40], b no band -> [18, 40] with the P18 note (merge notes). b's UFH:LFH% rows (#29) not entered: the merge notes rule the printed UFH:LFH ratio is not a catalogue measurement (do not compute ratios). (1) Interincisal angle, females 13 y, 125 ± 10: b only; Table III p. 22 prints it in the Miao females column -> kept (a missed it). (2) Gonial angle a same / b close -> close, points not stated (merge notes). (3) Selection a class-I / b class-I-balanced -> class-I-balanced: Class I occlusion with an attractive facial profile (text p. 21). (4) Table I's 7-year columns print no /1-MP or interincisal values (blank on p. 20). Page images: PDF pp. 2-6 = journal pp. 20-24 (Tables I-VI), rendered at 2000 px.

caveats: Quoted second-hand from Moate & Darendeliler 2002 (Aust Orthod J 18:19-26, a compilation of published Chinese cephalometric norms), Tables I, III and IV; the original paper was not read. The compilation rounds every mean and SD to whole numbers (Lew's soft tissue to 0.5) and gives no landmark, plane or method definitions.
The compilation states no film scale or magnification for any study; assumed true size (owner ruling M-2).

209 subjects with a Class I occlusion and an aesthetic facial profile, selected from 13,000 people in Guangzhou City, southern China; 104 males and 105 females aged 4 to 40 (text pp. 21-22). Group sizes per age and sex are not given; the sample n is the whole study.

Four age groups by physiological age and eruption status: 7, 9, 12.5 and 26.8 years (text p. 22). Entered by the table headers: 7 and 9 (Table I), 13 (Table III; the text says 12.5) and '18 Years +' (Table IV; 18-40 by convention).
Not entered (not catalogue measurements; no ratio computed): S-N (9 y, 63 ± 3), N-ANS and UFH:LFH% (every group).
Table V (p. 24) averages several studies; it is not entered for this study (merge notes).
